  <div class="prose">
    <p>
      I'm a PhD student at Northeastern, in the Data, Networks, and Algorithms Lab.
      I work on large language models: how to run them across several machines, including small ones, and how to change something they know without retraining the whole model.
    </p>
    <p class="mast-links">
      <a href="./research.qmd">Research</a>

    </p>

  </div>

  <section class="block">
    <h2>Work</h2>
    <p class="lede">A few things I'm working on right now.</p>

    <div class="entries">
      <div class="entry">
        <h3>Resilience for distributed language models</h3>
        <p>This continues JARVIS, which splits a language model across several devices. We added a way for the remaining devices to cover for one that drops out. We tried it with Gemma-2B on 18 radios in the Colosseum testbed, and on seven Raspberry Pis.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="entry">
        <h3>Communication-aware pruning</h3>
        <p>Training a neural network so that, once it is split across machines, those machines have to send less to each other, without losing accuracy.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="entry">
        <h3>Editing what a language model knows</h3>
        <p>Looking for cheaper ways to correct one fact in a language model, without retraining it and without undoing everything else it already knows.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>
